title: They Tortured The Wrong Man For Years . . . Then The DNA Test Came Back
caption:
Memories of Murder (2003): a village detective beats a confession out of a slow boy while a serial killer keeps striking in 1986 Korea. Then a Seoul detective arrives, and a DNA test from America changes everything. 😳 Follow for more movie recaps!

#memoriesofmurder #bongjoonho #movierecap #kmovie #spoilerroom
comment: Peter walked free. Was he the killer, or did Ryan almost shoot an innocent man? Why? 👀

segments.say: Ryan has a gun in a man's face. Then the DNA papers from America say *no match*.
To see how it got here, go back to *1986*.
A farmer finds a girl's body in a *drain*, deep in the rice fields.
Jack, the local detective, runs in. So do half the village and a damn *tractor*.
Jack has no training and no lab. He trusts one thing. His *eyes*.
Then a gossip points him at a slow, harmless boy named *Tommy*.
Jack and his partner Mike drag Tommy in, and beat him until he *breaks*.
They show him a footprint that matches his shoe. Tommy starts to *crack*.
So they drive him to the woods and feed him every answer. Tommy acts out the *murder*.
That was Jack's first mistake.
Watching from the trees is a young detective from Seoul. His name is *Ryan*.
Ryan believes in files, not gut. During a blackout drill, he sneaks into the records room, hunting for *proof*.
The next day, Jack stages a huge re-enactment for the *press*.
Then Tommy's father breaks through the *crowd*.

segments.text: He didn't kill anyone! My son's innocent!

segments.say: The case collapses. The newspapers tear the whole station *apart*.
Ryan keeps digging. Rain. Red clothes. Young women. One *killer*.
He marks a map, and the third body turns up right where he *said*.
Ryan was right. Jack hates that.
Over drinks that night, the two men finally *explode*.
The Chief pulls them apart. The killer will strike again, he says, on the next rainy *night*.
So officer Anna puts on a red skirt and goes out alone, as *bait*.
But the killer strikes somewhere else. By morning, all that's left is her *umbrella*.
And footprints, smeared by the *rain*.
Then Anna notices something. A song called Sad Letter plays on the radio before every *murder*.
Someone keeps mailing the radio show, asking for that song on rainy *nights*.
Jack gets desperate. He decides the killer has no body hair, so his men raid public *saunas*.
Desperate men chase desperate ideas.
Jack even visits a shaman, hoping she can show him a *face*.
Days later, the team chases a stranger through the night, all the way to a *quarry*.
Jack corners the man there. His name is *Sam*.
Sam has kids at home. But Jack trusts his *eyes*.
Jack and Mike break Sam, until he *dreams up* a confession.
That confession was worth *nothing*.
Meanwhile, Ryan follows a lead to a school, and hears about a crying *woman*.
He finds her. She is a *survivor*.
She never saw his face. But she remembers his *hands*.
Ryan runs back to stop it. Jack is about to *sign*.
Ryan blocks him, and the whole station *erupts*.
That same night, another girl is *dead*. And Sam was in a cell the whole time.
At last a postcard leads them to a quiet factory worker named *Peter*.
Peter has soft, clean hands. He started this town job just before the first *murder*.
He admits he sent the postcards. He swears he knows nothing about the *murders*.
Ryan describes the killer's night in horrible detail. Peter does not *flinch*.
This man is ice *cold*.
Back at the station, Jack can't sleep. How did Tommy know every detail? He digs out the old *tape*.
Tommy never confessed. On that tape, he sounds like a *witness*.
So they hunt Tommy down by the railway, and show him a photo of *Peter*.
Tommy stares at the photo. Then a train comes, and he is standing on the *tracks*.
Their only witness is gone. Their last hope is DNA, and Korea cannot test it. It has to go to *America*.
Then Mike steps on a rusty nail, and loses his *leg*.
Jack calls the post office every *hour*.
Peter slips away from the men watching him, and gets off the bus *early*.
Then another girl is killed in the *rain*.
Ryan snaps. He drags Peter into a train tunnel, and beats him on the *tracks*.
He pulls a gun, and screams for a *confession*.
Then the papers from America arrive. The DNA does *not match*.
Ryan says the document is a *lie*.
Jack holds Ryan back. Peter walks off into the *tunnel*. Years of work, gone.
Seventeen years later, Jack is a salesman with a *family*.
One day he drives past the same rice field, and *stops*.
He looks into the old drain, just like he did in *1986*.
A little girl is watching him.
She says a man was here not long ago, looking into the same *hole*.
Jack asks what he looked like.
The killer is still out there. And he could be *anyone*.
